fatal_errors: The as-deposited material is incorrectly assumed to be an ordered, grain-boundary-rich hexagonal phase; the target films and nanoribbons are amorphous or extremely fine/disordered with only cubic-type short-range order.
The proposed first-order magnetostructural-transition mechanism is not applicable to the as-deposited target state.

Annealing is incorrectly framed as reducing grain-boundary density. At 700 K there is no detectable grain growth or crystallization; the relevant mediator is short-range atomic reordering and relaxation of fabrication-induced strain.
The baseline claim of a sharp, large, strongly hysteretic magnetocaloric response conflicts with the observed broad, modest response of the as-deposited nanoribbons.
No prior observations or cited evidence are supplied to support the assumed microstructure and mechanism.
explanation: The response identifies post-deposition annealing and proposes a paired magnetic/structural test, which gives limited alignment with the target intervention. However, its central structural premise, baseline, and mechanism are incompatible with the target system. The actual 700 K treatment preserves the amorphous, short-range-ordered matrix while producing short-range relaxation, increased ferromagnetic alignment, higher magnetization, and a modest increase in peak −ΔSM from about 1.25 to 1.35 J kg−1 K−1. Broadening and reduced hysteresis were not the principal demonstrated outcomes. The response also omits the specified annealing conditions, elastic-strain and ribbon-spacing controls, field/temperature ranges, inverse response below 20 K, and the pre-crystallization boundary. Its experiment could test its own grain-boundary hypothesis, but it would not cleanly distinguish the target short-range-reordering mechanism unless TEM/SAED establishes the absence of grains and magnetization isotherms are compared before and after 700 K annealing.
